changes.before: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in October suggests that economic activity is expanding at a moderate pace.
changes.after: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace.

changes.before: Labor market conditions improved further, with solid job gains and a lower unemployment rate.
changes.after: Labor market conditions have improved further, with strong job gains and a lower unemployment rate.

changes.before: The Committee sees this guidance as consistent with its previous statement that it likely will be appropriate to maintain the 0 to 1/4 percent target range for the federal funds rate for a considerable time following the end of its asset purchase program in October, especially if projected inflation continues to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run goal, and provided that longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored.
Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's longer-run objective, partly reflecting declines in energy prices. Market-based measures of inflation compensation have declined somewhat further;
changes.after: Inflation has declined further below the Committee’s longer-run objective, largely reflecting declines in energy prices. Market-based measures of inflation compensation have declined substantially in recent months;

changes.before: The Committee expects inflation to rise gradually toward 2 percent as the labor market improves further
changes.after: Inflation is anticipated to decline further in the near term, but the Committee expects inflation to rise gradually toward 2 percent over the medium term as the labor market improves further
and readings on financial and international developments.
recent declines in energy prices have boosted household purchasing power.

parsed.rationale: The upgrade of growth to 'solid' and job gains to 'strong', plus dropping the 'considerable time' link, tilt the statement toward earlier normalization. Weaker inflation language and the added international developments partly offset this, so the net shift is modestly hawkish.

spans.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in October suggests that economic activity is expanding at a moderate pace.
Labor market conditions improved further, with solid job gains and a lower unemployment rate.

The Committee sees this guidance as consistent with its previous statement that it likely will be appropriate to maintain the 0 to 1/4 percent target range for the federal funds rate for a considerable time following the end of its asset purchase program in October, especially if projected inflation continues to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run goal, and provided that longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored.
Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's longer-run objective, partly reflecting declines in energy prices. Market-based measures of inflation compensation have declined somewhat further;
The Committee expects inflation to rise gradually toward 2 percent as the labor market improves further
Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace.
Labor market conditions have improved further, with strong job gains and a lower unemployment rate.

Inflation has declined further below the Committee’s longer-run objective, largely reflecting declines in energy prices. Market-based measures of inflation compensation have declined substantially in recent months;
Inflation is anticipated to decline further in the near term, but the Committee expects inflation to rise gradually toward 2 percent over the medium term as the labor market improves further
and readings on financial and international developments.
recent declines in energy prices have boosted household purchasing power.
